title: ThAME: 3D Memory-Enabled Heterogeneous Accelerator for LLM Mixture of Experts
event_hint: ThAME: a proposed 3D heterogeneous multi-chiplet accelerator combining FeFET-NAND and DRAM memory chiplets with a co-designed hierarchical NoC for MoE LLM inference (architecture study, not silicon).
problem: MoE inference on conventional hardware is bottlenecked by three issues: massive memory bandwidth needed to fetch non-contiguous expert weights, non-deterministic scatter-gather traffic from input-dependent token routing, and tail-latency dependency from synchronous expert output aggregation. Expert weights dominate model size (>90%) and existing memory hierarchies cannot balance density, leakage and access latency.
mechanism: ThAME is a 3D heterogeneous multi-chiplet architecture using FeFET (ferroelectric FET) non-volatile and DRAM volatile memory chiplets with a co-designed compute mapping that aligns attention and expert routing profiles. It stores expert weights on-chip in 3D FeFET-NAND to break the memory wall, and adds a specialized hierarchical Network-on-Chip (designed via Archived Multi-Objective Simulated Annealing, AMOSA) inside the FeFET-NAND die to mitigate non-deterministic token-routing traffic. Evaluated config: two FeFET and two DRAM memory chiplets plus a systolic-array (TPU v6e) host chiplet on a silicon interposer, point-to-point connected.

evidence.claim: ThAME outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts by up to 15.7x speedup and improves energy efficiency by up to 9.8x.
evidence.value: up to 15.7x speedup; up to 9.8x energy efficiency
evidence.condition: abstract headline; detailed baseline/workload in results

evidence.claim: ThAME delivers 147.5 Tokens/s/W, a 5.6x, 20.9x and 31.7x improvement over Stratum, TPU v6e and NVIDIA A100 baselines respectively; normalized by silicon area it reaches 184.3 Tokens/s/kW/mm^2.

At batch size B=64 (Deepseek model, MMLU), ThAME delivers up to 5.92x and 12.77x higher throughput than Stratum and H3D-T respectively; the gap widens with batch size due to Stratum/H3D-T network contention.

Co-design decomposition: swapping ThAME's hierarchical NoC for a Mesh topology degrades latency up to 1.44x and energy efficiency up to 2.1x; substituting FeFET-NAND with DRAM-PNM adds up to 1.8x energy overhead; synergistic co-design yields 4.7x/7.0x latency and 5.4x/8.7x energy efficiency gains over Stratum for Qwen1.5 and Deepseek respectively.

Evaluation uses cycle-accurate simulators: SCALE-Sim for systolic array latency (median error <3% vs production TPU), NeuroSim for FeFET-NAND 3D arrays (chip-level error <1% after calibration), BookSim2 for intra-chiplet NoC, HotSpot for thermal; 16-bit fixed-point precision; MoE models Deepseek-16B, Olmoe-1B, Qwen1.5-2.7B, Qwen3-30B and dense Llama3-8B.
evidence.condition: 45C ambient, 50W base die budget, 4096 PEs/core, 32-core system, 121mm^2 base die
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 8 - Experimental Setup

evaluation_context: Architecture study evaluated entirely via cycle-accurate simulation (SCALE-Sim, NeuroSim, BookSim2, HotSpot), not taped-out silicon. 16-bit fixed-point precision. Config: 2 FeFET + 2 DRAM chiplets + TPU v6e host on silicon interposer, 32-core/4096-PE system, 121mm^2 base die, 50W base-die thermal budget at 45C ambient. Baselines: Stratum (DRAM-PNM), H3D-T (3D FeFET/SRAM/TPU), TPU v6e, NVIDIA A100. MoE workloads: Deepseek-16B, Olmoe-1B, Qwen1.5-2.7B, Qwen3-30B; dense Llama3-8B.
limitations: Results are simulation-based (cycle-accurate modeling, calibrated but not silicon measurements); no real chip, no deployment. HBF reference (SK Hynix H^3 up to 2.69x throughput-per-watt) is cited as related context, not a ThAME measurement. The evaluated chiplet count/config is one specific point; authors note it does not affect generalizability but other configs are not shown. Decode-phase token latency and end-to-end serving P95 are not reported; metrics focus on speedup, energy efficiency, Tokens/s/W and throughput scaling. FeFET device variability/endurance is acknowledged as a memory-technology trade-off but not quantified in results.
project_relevance: ThAME directly addresses the MoE memory-wall and intra-chiplet routing problem relevant to AI accelerator architecture and memory-IO codesign: it couples high-density 3D FeFET-NAND storage with a specialized NoC. For the project card it is a simulation-stage architecture proposal (not pre-silicon validation or production), so its system claims are architectural projections rather than measured silicon. The HBF/FeFET angle also touches the storage-media question of whether NAND-based near-memory compute can enter the AI memory hierarchy.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.17074v2 (19 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source.
All performance numbers come from cycle-accurate simulation (SCALE-Sim/NeuroSim/BookSim2/HotSpot), not silicon.
Baselines are explicitly named: Stratum, H3D-T, TPU v6e, NVIDIA A100.
